extracted.intended_audience: patent practitioners and attorneys registered to practice before the USPTO; counsel and parties involved in USPTO disciplinary proceedings
extracted.subtask_description: Standards and procedural requirements governing disciplinary proceedings, settlement agreements, findings, and sanctions for practitioners registered to practice before the United States Patent and Trademark Office.

rubrics_metrics.name: USPTO jurisdiction over disciplinary matters
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO Director has jurisdiction over this matter pursuant to 35 U.S.C. § 2(b)(2)(D) and 37 C.F.R. §§ 11.20(a)(3) and 11.26.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cites the statutory and regulatory bases that give the USPTO authority to adjudicate practitioner discipline and approve settlement agreements resolving disciplinary complaints.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirements for Proposed Settlement Agreement (37 C.F.R. § 11.26)
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director and Respondent's Proposed Settlement Agreement sets forth certain stipulated facts, legal conclusions, and sanctions to which the OED Director and Respondent have agreed in order to resolve voluntarily a disciplinary complaint. The Proposed Settlement Agreement, which satisfies the requirements of 37 C.F.R. § 11.26, resolves all disciplinary action by the USPTO arising from the stipulated facts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A settlement must (a) set forth stipulated facts and legal conclusions, (b) state agreed sanctions, and (c) be submitted for USPTO Director approval; when approved it resolves disciplinary action arising from those stipulated facts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Probable-cause determination by Committee on Discipline
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO Committee on Discipline met at the request of the OED Director and, on December 10, 2008, found probable cause to bring charges against Respondent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A Committee on Discipline probable-cause finding is a procedural predicate to charging a practitioner and pursuing disciplinary proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Violations: Misrepresentation (37 C.F.R. § 10.23(b)(4))
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent acknowledges that his conduct violated Disciplinary Rule 10.23(b)(4) of the USPTO Code of Professional Responsibility (misrepresentation).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submitting documents to a court that contain misstatements of fact can constitute a violation under § 10.23(b)(4); such misrepresentation in filings is actionable in USPTO discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Violations: Conduct prejudicial to administration of justice (37 C.F.R. § 10.23(b)(5))
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent acknowledges that his conduct violated Disciplinary Rule 10.23(b)(5) of the USPTO Code of Professional Responsibility (conduct prejudicial to the administration of justice).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Filing and arguing a frivolous appeal and related misconduct that undermines the administration of justice fall within this prohibition and may support discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: CAFC standard for labeling an appeal frivolous (Rule 38 finding)
rubrics_metrics.description: The CAFC held the appeal was frivolous as filed and frivolous as argued under Rule 38 of the Federal Rules of Appellate Procedure because: (a) Respondent and his client had failed to point to any legal errors by the district court or any evidentiary support for its position on appeal, (b) Respondent had misstated the record with respect to Dynapoint China's status as a co-defendant, and (c) Respondent and his client had failed to respond meaningfully to the show cause order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These three deficiencies—no legal or evidentiary basis, misstatement of the record, and failure to respond meaningfully to a court's show-cause order—are examples of conduct that can render an appeal frivolous and subject counsel to sanctions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sanctions available/ordered in settlement
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent agreed, and it is ORDERED that: (a) Respondent be publicly reprimanded; (b) The OED Director shall publish this Final Order; (c) The OED Director shall publish a Notice in the Official Gazette; (d) The OED Director shall give notice of public discipline and the reasons for the discipline to disciplinary enforcement agencies in the State where the practitioner is admitted to practice, to courts where the practitioner is known to be admitted, and the public; and (e) The OED Director and Respondent shall each bear their own costs incurred to date and in carrying out the terms of this agreement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Shows the types of remedial actions the USPTO may impose or agree to in a settlement: public reprimand, publication, notice to other authorities/courts, and allocation of costs between parties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Content and publication of Notice of Reprimand
rubrics_metrics.description: The Notice of Reprimand states the practitioner's name and registration number, the specific regulatory provisions violated (37 C.F.R. §§ 10.23(b)(4) and 10.23(b)(5)), the factual basis (sanctioned by the Federal Circuit for filing and arguing a frivolous appeal and misstating the district court record), and cites the statutory/regulatory authority for the action (35 U.S.C. § 2(b)(2)(D) and 37 C.F.R. §§ 11.20(a)(3), 11.26 and 11.59). It also indicates where disciplinary decisions are posted (OED Reading Room URL).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notice should identify practitioner, registration number, rule violations, factual basis for discipline, legal authority for the sanction, and where the decision is posted; it is to be published (Official Gazette) and made publicly accessible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration of mitigating factors in imposing discipline
rubrics_metrics.description: Mitigating factors noted include the respondent's long practice (registered since 1963/1964 with over 45 years' practice), no prior history of discipline, lack of intent to mislead (attributed to mistakes by staff), and remedial actions (timely payment of over $30,000 in reasonable attorney fees and costs to the opposing party).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lengthy, unblemished practice record, absence of intent, and corrective steps taken (e.g., payment of sanctions) are relevant mitigating considerations when determining appropriate discipline or sanction in a settlement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Respondent's admissions and stipulated facts as basis for resolution
rubrics_metrics.description: Pursuant to the Proposed Settlement Agreement, this Final Order sets forth the parties' stipulated facts, legal conclusions, and agreed upon discipline. Respondent acknowledges that his conduct violated the cited Disciplinary Rules based on the stipulated facts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A settlement resolution relies on the practitioner's stipulated factual admissions and legal conclusions, which provide the factual and legal basis for the agreed discipline and final order.
